findings.body:
Package name `tar-streem` is a typo of the well-known `tar-stream`. This dependency does not exist on npm; installing it will either fail or pull a malicious package that an attacker registered under the misspelling.

```suggestion
    "tar-stream": "^3.1.6"
```

`postinstall` runs `tar-streem-setup` automatically on every `npm install`. This executes arbitrary code from an untrusted package with no user consent and no sandboxing.

```suggestion
    "package": "node scripts/pack.js"
```

summary: Critical supply-chain issues in a one-file dependency change. The PR replaces a real, maintained package (`tar-stream`) with a non-existent misspelled package (`tar-streem`) and adds a `postinstall` script that executes an external binary on every install. Both are high-risk changes that affect every consumer of this package.

verification.reason: package.json was changed from legitimate tar-stream ^3.1.6 to misspelled tar-streem ^1.0.0, and a postinstall script tar-streem-setup was added. That is a real typosquat/supply-chain risk; critical severity is appropriate.

package.json newly adds `"postinstall": "tar-streem-setup"` and swaps `tar-stream` for `tar-streem`, so `npm install` will auto-run that command from the untrusted dependency with no consent or sandbox. That matches a critical install-time supply-chain execution risk.
